Dear Hedgeye Subscriber,

Another #Quad4 week is in the books. More turmoil in financial markets.

Shares of PacWest (PACW) plunged more than -20% on Thursday after reporting in an SEC filing that heightened customer "fears of the safety of their deposits" led to a drop in deposits of 9.5% in the prior week (between May 4th and 5th). (Quick takeaway: The banking crisis isn’t over.)

So while the large cap Tech companies are all talking about how AI will transform their businesses (Google mentioned “AI” 143x at their analyst day) the rest of America is firmly grounded in near-term reality. Did we mention NFIB Small Business Optimism hit new cycle lows this week?

(Reminder: Small Businesses make up 99.9% of all businesses in the U.S. and account for 45% to 50% of U.S. GDP.) 

Similarly, the Russell 2000 (a lot of stocks) is still down almost -29% from its November 2021 highs and only +6% off its June 2022 lows. So yes, the S&P 500 is top-heavy with Apple (AAPL) contributing greater than 30% of the S&P 500’s 7% YTD return. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (RSP) is -0.3% YTD. (This is just another way of saying a small group of the largest cap stocks are doing all the heavy lifting for the SPY.)

All is not well inside the U.S. economy.

A final concerning development here: Policymakers are at a stalemate about the U.S. Debt Ceiling, as our D.C. policy team reminded us this week. “They are no closer to an agreement than when they walked into that room at 4:00 yesterday. Period,” Macro Policy analyst JT Taylor said on “The Call @ Hedgeye” this week.

That’s concerning when you consider the timeline over which the debt ceiling needs to get done. “There has to be a deal, then a committee process and then legislation all in 15 short days,” JT continues. JT thinks we’re in Round 3 of a fight that will last for another 4, 5, or 6 rounds. Meanwhile, U.S. Credit Default Swaps continue to hit new cycle highs.

So what’s a savvy investor to do? For one thing, the halfway point of 2Q 2023 is fast approaching. And our Founder and Risk-Manager-In-Chief Keith McCullough will provide an update on this slow-moving Quad 4 crash in his Mid-Quarter Macro Themes presentation at 11 a.m. ET Wednesday.

Macro Pro and Institutional subscribers get exclusive insight into McCullough’s investing outlook before anyone else. This presentation includes our updated 150+-page “Global Macro Outlook” slide deck and the resulting investment conclusions.

Regardless of whether you upgrade or not, here’s a reminder of our 2Q 2023 Macro Themes, that Keith and the Macro team will discuss on this Mid-Quarter Update call:

										Quad4 Profit Recession Reiterated: New Quarter, Same TREND as the slowest-moving Quad 4 wreck in modernity continues to soldier southward. Lost pricing power, tighter credit, contracting liquidity, negative real income growth, deteriorating real discretionary consumption capacity and rolling credit events continue to define the local (and global) macro trajectory, and the trajectory of the domestic profit cycle by extension. We’ll detail the fragility and trap door risk associated with the progressive hollowing out of underlying conditions and update the outlook and risk management playbook as Phase III of the Bear Market remains in conspicuous motion.

										 

										#Quad4 Credit Event Reiterated: The stressors of Quad 4 have been building for some time and the pressure in the system has reached a critical threshold. Bank runs triggered by long-duration assets funded with fickle, uninsured liabilities are simply the latest symptom. The next phase of the credit cycle will reflect further tightening in credit availability and deteriorating credit quality at both the household and commercial level. Still-too-high inflation coupled with persistent labor market imbalances and that will keep the pressures in the system simmering. So long as Quad 4 remains the trajectory and cost, availability and quality of credit continue to deteriorate, credit event risk will simply remain a when, not an if.

										 

										Long Gold Reiterated: Any port in a storm? How about the Quad 4 port trifecta of Gold, $USD, Duration. While most commodity prices have been collapsing under Quad 4 demand destruction (oil, anyone?), gold has been doing what it should do in Quad 4 … a) not lose value and b) push slowly, steadily higher. While the full economic fallout of policy mismanagement has yet to play out, the downstream reaction function is increasingly coming into focus. Not only is Gold a port in the storm, but investors know the policy reaction function down the road will be to print. Knowing this, Gold reacts accordingly.

Hedgeye Risk Management is an independent investment research and online financial media company, focused exclusively on generating and delivering thoughtful investment ideas in a proven buy-side process. The firm combines quantitative, bottom-up and macro analysis with an emphasis on timing.  

The Hedgeye team features some of the most highly-regarded research analysts on Wall Street, covering Macro, Financials, Energy, Healthcare, Retail, Gaming, Lodging & Leisure (GLL), Restaurants, Industrials, Consumer Staples, Internet & Media, Housing, Materials, Technology, Demography and Washington policy analysis, including Macro, Energy, Healthcare, Telecom & Media and Defense.
